item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fiji Bati have opened their Rugby League World Cup campaign with a convincing 40-12 victory over the Cook Islands at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

The Bati scored seven tries, with Waqa Blake, Jacob Saifiti, Taane Milne, Caleb Navale and Kitione Kautoga crossing the try line, while Solomone Saukuru scored a double.

The Bati applied pressure on the Cook Islands from the beginning of the match, launching wave after wave of attacks and maintaining their intensity throughout the game.

Bati captain Apisai Koroisau says they knew they had to start fast and praised the players for their efforts on the field.

Koroisau says the team knew what they needed to do in the first half and executed their game plan well.

With Australia up next, Koroisau says the Kangaroos are at the top of the food chain for a reason, but the Bati will give everything they have on the field.

Wakeham was named Player of the Match after producing three try assists, two line breaks and four tackle breaks, alongside an impressive kicking performance.

The Bati will face the Kangaroos at Suncorp Stadium at 9.05pm next Sunday.

item.title: SODELPA warns proposed constitutional changes could delay elections by up to 12 months
item.description: The Social Democratic Liberal Party is raising concerns that proposed changes to Fiji's Constitution, could allow Parliament's term to be extended by up to 12 months during a state of emergency, potentially delaying elections. SODELPA is calling on the Special Parliamentary Select Committee and Cabinet, to urgently review Sections 201 and 202 of the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 to safeguard
item.content:encoded:
The Social Democratic Liberal Party is raising concerns that proposed changes to Fiji's Constitution, could allow Parliament's term to be extended by up to 12 months during a state of emergency, potentially delaying elections.

SODELPA is calling on the Special Parliamentary Select Committee and Cabinet, to urgently review Sections 201 and 202 of the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 to safeguard people's democratic rights and freedoms.

The party says under Sections 201(3) and (4), if a state of emergency is declared towards the end of Parliament's term, the President, acting on Cabinet's advice, could extend the parliamentary term by up to 12 months.

SODELPA is concerned this could allow a government to remain in power beyond the normal parliamentary term without an election.

While acknowledging the need for emergency powers to respond to natural disasters, health crises and security threats, the party says these should not interfere with people's right to vote.

They also point out that the 2013 Constitution did not provide a mechanism for Cabinet to extend Parliament's four-year term during a state of emergency.

SODELPA is calling for Sections 201(3) and (4) to be removed from the Bill to ensure Parliament's term remains fixed and elections are held as scheduled.

The party has also raised concerns about Section 202, which it says could allow restrictions on certain rights and freedoms during a state of emergency.

These include freedom of speech, assembly and movement, personal privacy and access to information.

SODELPA warns that such powers could be misused to prevent people from speaking out, holding peaceful gatherings or questioning government decisions.

They also want freedom of speech, assembly and movement to be protected from suspension during a state of emergency.

The party stresses that it supports changes to the 2013 Constitution but believes any amendments must safeguard democracy and the rights of all Fijians.

SODELPA is also urging the Government to provide clear and accurate information, about the proposed changes so people can make informed decisions.

They say the constitutional review process must be handled carefully to protect people's rights and avoid unnecessary instability.

item.title: Sporting body Chair leaves Fiji amid investigation into alleged sexual harassment
item.description: The Chairman of a sporting body who has been under police investigation over alleged sexual harassment has left Fiji to join his team in Australia ahead of a major tournament. item.content:encoded:
The Chairman of a sporting body who has been under police investigation over alleged sexual harassment has left Fiji to join his team in Australia ahead of a major tournament.

Police have confirmed to fijivillage News that the person of interest has been interviewed and released, with investigators now compiling the investigation file to be forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions for independent legal advice.

The victim has reached out to the Fiji Women's Crisis Centre for assistance in seeking justice.

It is understood that the person of interest provided police with a medical sheet, prompting inves tigato rs to put the case on hold until he recovered .

He was later allowed to join the team in Australia just days before a tournament.

The victim's family is now questioning how the investigation was handled and why the person of interest was allowed to leave the country while the allegations remain under investigation.

The family is also seeking clarity on whether he will return to Fiji to answer questions relating to the allegations.

item.title: Naivalurua calls for an end to abusive and humiliating social media posts
item.description: People are being reminded to stop sharing abusive and humiliating content on social media. Minister for Policing and Communications Ioane Naivalurua says he is concerned about the increasingly degrading and abusive material being published online.
item.content:encoded:
People are being reminded to stop sharing abusive and humiliating content on social media.

Minister for Policing and Communications Ioane Naivalurua says he is concerned about the increasingly degrading and abusive material being published online.

Naivalurua says personal attacks, cruel comments, humiliating photos and videos, and graphic content are being shared with little thought for the people affected.

The Minister says too often, another person's embarrassment or suffering is treated as entertainment.

Naivalurua says this must stop, as the trauma caused can continue long after a post has been deleted.

He is urging everyone to stop posting, sharing and forwarding intimate or degrading content.

He says parents, teachers, community leaders and all social media users have a part to play in preventing online abuse.

If you are affected by online harm and require assistance then you can contact the Online Safety Commission on 1548 .

item.title: Police urge parents to monitor children following concerns along Khalsa Road
item.description: Police are urging parents to monitor their children's whereabouts following concerns raised about young people gathering along Khalsa Road in the evenings. A concerned resident has told fijivillage News that children, including girls wearing school uniforms, have been seen in the area after 8pm without adult supervision.
item.content:encoded:
Police are urging parents to monitor their children's whereabouts following concerns raised about young people gathering along Khalsa Road in the evenings.

A concerned resident has told fijivillage News that children, including girls wearing school uniforms, have been seen in the area after 8pm without adult supervision.

The resident also claims some young people have been seen sniffing glue and fighting, raising concerns about their safety.

In response to questions from fijivillage News, Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe has reminded parents and guardians to make their children's safety a priority.

Vusonilawe says parents must know where their children are, who they are spending time with, and ensure they return home safely.

He is also urging parents to make sure their children do not get involved with the wrong crowd.
